independent.summary: The caps are applied in UTF-16 code units (`clip` uses `text.length`) while the bound the tests assert is in bytes (`MAX_RECORD_BYTES = 2048`, and the same literal in server/tests/http/mcp.test.js:742). Every hostile case is built from ASCII ('x'/'z' repeats), so the new 512-char `source` ceiling is never exercised with multi-byte text: a `session_missing` request whose `method` is ~500 BMP multi-byte characters (3 bytes each) yields ~1.5 kB of `source` alone, and combined with a maxed `ua`/`client`/`ip`/`rpc`/`requestId` the record reaches ~2.9 kB — past the ceiling the test file claims holds 'whatever the request was'. The module's own promise is phrased in characters, so this is a pre-existing char-vs-byte mismatch the new 512 ceiling widens rather than a new unbounded hole; the record is still bounded, just at a larger constant than the tests pin.
